deep.reconstruction:
This is not a mathematical page. It continues the previous page's list 'Geburtsjahre Göttingischer Professoren' (birth dates of Göttingen professors), and the bottom half adds colleagues, assistants, astronomers and mathematicians.

Structure of the entries (inferred by me from internal consistency):

(a) Name, birth year, birth day.

(b) A two-digit number, which is the age at appointment to Göttingen. Examples:
- Hausmann 1782, 29: came 1811.
- Dissen 1784, 29: 1813.
- Weber 1804, 27: 1831.
- K. O. Müller 1797, 22: 1819.
- Wendt 1783, 46: 1829.
- Dahlmann 1785, 44: 1829.
- Lücke 1792, 35: 1827.
- On the previous page, Gauss 1777, 30: 1807.

(c) Date of death, marked †.

(d) A five-digit number, which is the length of life in days. On the previous page these form the column 27915, 29242, ... (also visible as the left margin here). On this page there is one such number, 26560, written above the Oesterley entry.

The only computation on this page is therefore implicit: the lifespan of G. H. Oesterley in days. He was born 24 Oct 1774 and died 14 Jul 1847. My reconstruction of the count:
- 1774-10-24 to 1846-10-24 is 72 years.
- 72·365 = 26280 days.
- There are 17 intervening Feb-29s, since 1800 is not a leap year in the Gregorian calendar. This gives 26297.
- 1846-10-24 to 1847-07-14 is 31+30+31+31+28+31+30+31+20 = 263 days.
- Total: 26297 + 263 = 26560, exactly Gauss's figure.

The same method checks exactly on the previous page:
- Euler, 15 Apr 1707 to 18 Sep 1783: 76·365 + 19 + 156 = 27915.
- Lagrange, 25 Jan 1736 to 10 Apr 1813: 28124 + 75 = 28199.
- Stromeyer, 4 Jun 1750 to 27 Jun 1830: 29219 + 23 = 29242. This also confirms the uncertain death day as June 27.
- Newton: 30766 comes out exactly using Old-Style (Julian) dates, 25 Dec 1642 to 20 Mar 1727.

The right column gives birth dates (and some birthplaces) of others: Gerling, Encke, Bessel, Hansen (Tondern), Listing, Sartorius von Waltershausen and his wife, Jacobi (Potsdam), Dirichlet (Düren) and von Lindenau (Altenburg). Under Ewald, 'Frau 1822 März 23' is a wife's birth date; this is plausibly his second wife, Auguste Schleiermacher, which is my inference. Later additions in other hands or inks include Riemann 1826 and Gould 1824; Enneper 1830 Jun 14 is in faint pencil, in a later hand.

The purpose is personal and actuarial-statistical: tracking ages and exact days lived of colleagues. This fits Gauss's documented interest in mortality and life-expectancy data and his habit of counting days lived.
errors: No arithmetic error detected: 26560 for Oesterley checks exactly, as do the previous-page figures 27915 (Euler), 28199 (Lagrange) and 29242 (Stromeyer).
Possible slip, unsure: 'Nicolai 1794'. The astronomer F. B. G. Nicolai was born 25 Oct 1793, if this is he; the entry is faint and may refer to someone else.
The 'franz Eichhorn 1786 Oct. 7' entry is uncertain in both name and date; I cannot confirm the person.

results.what: Computation of exact lifespans in days from Gregorian birth and death dates, correctly omitting the 1800 leap day. For Newton, Julian dates are evidently used.
results.modern_name: Day-count / Julian-day-number difference; elementary calendar arithmetic
results.usually_credited_to: Routine (Scaliger's Julian period; standard astronomical practice)

results.what: Compilation of ages at appointment and longevity of Göttingen professors (mortality statistics)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss's interest in mortality tables and widows' funds is well documented (Göttingen Professoren-Witwenkasse work, 1840s)

deep.surprise_reason: Biographical and calendar data with routine day-count arithmetic. It is a nice confirmation of Gauss's known habit of computing lifespans in days and his actuarial interests, but it contains no mathematics beyond calendar arithmetic.

checkable.asserts: Oesterley's lifespan in days equals Gauss's 26560
Euler's lifespan in days (previous page / left margin)
Stromeyer (sen.) lifespan; confirms death date June 27, 1830
Hand reconstruction of the Oesterley count (17 leap days, 1800 excluded)
Second numeric column = age at appointment (Hausmann, Weber, Dahlmann)

transcription_corrections: 'Jul. 10' after Gerling 1788 is correct (C. L. Gerling, b. 10 July 1788).
The '44' at the right margin belongs to Dahlmann (age 44 at his 1829 appointment), and '|46|' belongs to Wendt (1829 appointment).
'|35' after Lücke is his age at appointment (1827); the trailing '2' is uncertain.
'Julius 22' before Bessel should read 'Julius 22' / 'Jul 22' (Bessel b. 22 July 1784).
Under Hansen, 'Tondern' is his birthplace; similarly 'Potsdam' (Jacobi), 'Düren' (Dirichlet) and 'Altenburg' (v. Lindenau) are birthplaces.
Saalfeld note: 'zu Korb Oberamt Weiblingen', i.e. Waiblingen (place of death).
The number '26560' above the Focke/Oesterley lines is Oesterley's lifespan in days (bracketed to his entry).
Lünemann's death mark '† (..)' is illegible; the second '†' sits beside Müller 1783.
'Frl. W. Böbes' is uncertain; the reading is doubtful.
'Enneper 1830 Jun 14' is a later pencil addition in a different hand, not Gauss's.
In 'Meierstein 180[8]', the year digit is overwritten (8 over another digit); likely Moritz Meyerstein, instrument maker, b. 1808. Similarly, 'Benedict Listing 1808 Jul 25' has an overwritten 8.
